html:
The Matawai are a Maroon people of Suriname, living along the Saramacca River. They descend from Africans who escaped from slavery on Dutch plantations near the coast in the 1700s and built free villages in the rainforest.

The map shows their area in 1492, before they existed; at that time it was the land of Carib and Arawak-speaking peoples such as the Kalina and the Lokono.

The Matawai split off from the larger Saramaka Maroons. After years of war, the Dutch colony of Surinam made peace treaties with the Maroons in the 1760s, and the Matawai gained their freedom in return for promising not to shelter new runaways. Like other Maroons they kept many West African ways, brought by the Atlantic slave trade, in religion, farming and government. A few thousand live in Suriname today.
